title: Why 2025 Is a Gold Rush Year for Business Buyers

 Why 2025 Is a Gold Rush Year for Business Buyers
Hi Sara,
There’s a perfect storm brewing in the business world—and for once, it’s good news.
2025 has been the biggest year ever for small business acquisitions, and no, that’s not just LinkedIn hype. I’m on the front lines as a deal attorney to small deals, and what I’m seeing is a tidal wave of buyers and sellers finally meeting in the middle. 
Here's why:
1. Boomers Are Out (and There Are a Lot of Them)
Call it the “silver tsunami” if you must, but Baby Boomers are done. Sellers in their 70s, 80s, even 90s are still hanging on, hoping to sell to the next generation… who mostly say, “Thanks, but no thanks.” That leaves a huge inventory of businesses with no succession plan. Opportunity is knocking.
2. Millennials and Gen X Want Freedom
Forget the corner office. This generation wants autonomy, flexibility, and control—not another round of soul-sucking meetings. Self-employment isn’t a fringe idea anymore—it’s a career goal.
3. The Startup Dream? Kinda Dead
Remember the “Uber for X” phase? Yeah, so do I. I represented a lot of those companies, and let me tell you—those glossy press releases rarely matched the reality (behind the scenes those billion dollar exits were rarely as exciting as they sound). Entrepreneurs are now wiser, more risk-averse, and looking for cash flow, not chaos.
4. Search Funds Are Booming
Entrepreneurship-through-acquisition is the new startup. You get to run a business, make it better, and skip the painful zero-to-one stage. It’s a safer bet for ambitious people who want ROI and can afford their life at the same time.
5. Real Estate’s Tough, Crypto’s Weird, Stocks Are Stressful
High interest rates have made real estate as an investment play less attractive. Crypto lost its edge now that it tracks the stock market. The stock market? Yawn. People want something tangible, profitable, and slightly less roller-coastery. Enter: small business acquisition.
6. Post-Pandemic Priorities Have Shifted
Working from home changed everything. People tasted freedom and liked it. Then came the return-to-office mandates, layoffs, and existential crises. Now, many are asking, “Why not just buy a business?” And they’re right to ask.
Bottom line?

We’ve got more sellers than ever. More buyers than ever. And more deals are happening than ever. It’s raining transactions in 2025.
If you’re thinking about buying (or selling) a business, now is not the time to sit on the sidelines. Head to Deal Academy to get expert insights, tools, and actual legal intel—not recycled Twitter threads, I swear.
To smarter deals and bold moves,
Sara Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
Founder, Deal Academy
